title: Bitwidth strategy sandbox / Console Optimize demo
summary: Redwood walkthrough of Optimize console focusing on bitwidth/quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Demoed QProfile selection, sandbox bench, latency vs quality heatmaps; discussed BlueCrest constraints (low-latency triage, PHI handling), proposed pilot: 2-week sandbox + accuracy tolerance matrix + pricing estimate for Dedicated pilot.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (BlueCrest Head of ML), Dan Wu (BlueCrest Infra), Liam O'Neill (CTO)
---
0:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick agenda: we want to walk through Optimize console, show qprofile selection, run through an int8 vs fp8 demo in the sandbox, and figure out next steps for a pilot.
0:12 Sara: thanks, glad to be here. our main thing is triage latency — the docs say 200ms p95 target and we need to see quality doesn't drop for diagnostic prompts.
0:20 Ethan: great, i'll drive the console tour and live bench. small note: we'll simulate BlueCrest prompts, but please do send your actual set after; the more representative the better.
1:05 Ethan: opening the Optimize console now — top left is the model selection, we have curated open models and then qprofile presets. you can see presets like "latency-first" (int8 biased), "fidelity-first" (fp8), and "hybrid" which uses adaptive fallback rules.
1:32 Dan: quick question, does hybrid actually switch mid-inference or only per-request?
1:36 Ethan: it's per-request and per-route policy; we maintain the kv cache across compatible variants so we avoid cold-start penalties. sometimes transcription will call it the K-V cash, i've seen that — it's the KV cache.
2:05 Maya: for BlueCrest you'd likely define a route for triage which pins to a low-latency qprofile and another route for deep-review which favors fidelity.
2:27 Liam: can we get a single endpoint and let Redwood route based on token budget? we don't want two different endpoints for simplicity.
2:34 Ethan: yes, routing rules can live in one endpoint — you can base routing on metadata (route keys), latency SLOs, or token budgets. we'll demo routing after the bench run.
3:10 Ethan: now switching to the sandbox. i'm loading a short prompt set — these are anonymized triage prompts (symptoms -> likely category + suggested escalation). note that in the console we show quality deltas with a tiled heatmap, the x axis is latency and the y is drop in key metric (here we used F1 on intent).
4:05 Ethan: starting int8 run. this is the INT8 quantized profile, higher batching, smaller kernels, we expect ~35-45% token cost savings but some drift on edge cases.
5:00 Speaker 1 (transcription): "so int 8 is like 8 bits uh but how often does it hallucinate?"
5:12 Sara: yeah like for very low-supporting context it can hallucinate or paraphrase wrong — can you show a failure mode?
5:18 Ethan: sure, i'll pull a couple of contrived prompts. okay prompt A: rare disease symptom description with lab values. int8 output: sees some small paraphrase that loses a numeric relation, FP8 keeps the relation. you can see the regressed score in the heatmap.
6:05 Ethan: note that the qprofile sensitivity sweep will run the prompt set across multiple quantization seeds and produce a delta table. it summarizes metrics like BLEU, F1, semantic similarity.
7:00 Dan: how do you compute semantic similarity? we use embed models internally and it's a little fuzzy.
7:12 Ethan: we use a paired-assessment approach by default (embedding + cosine + threshold) and we also support external eval hooks so you can plug your own clinical scorer.
8:03 Sara: what's the typical latency difference on our infra target? we'll be on GCP a2-type nodes for hosted soon, but Dedicated would be an option.
8:20 Maya: based on our public benchmarks, for conversational seq-lens ~128, INT8 on A2 gives p95 ~140-170ms, FP8 tends to be 180-240ms depending on kernel selection and batch. these are rough until we run your samples.
9:05 Sara: okay so int8 looks promising, but is the quality delta consistent across prompt classes?
9:15 Ethan: great question — often it's not uniform. e.g., templated prompts are safe, but free-form triage narratives and labs with numbers are more sensitive. that's why we recommend a sensitivity sweep and a fallback rule: if semantic similarity drops below threshold, route to higher-fidelity profile.
10:10 Liam: that fallback — is it automatic and synchronous? we can't accept double compute for p95 reasons.
10:20 Ethan: fallback is synchronous but optimized: we do a quick cheap check with a small proxy scorer and only escalate when necessary. for many workloads that's a small percent. we also offer canary rollouts so small fraction of traffic uses higher fidelity.
11:02 Dan: how about caching? we have a lot of repeated prefixes for triage triage flows, can we cache completions or kv?
11:18 Ethan: yes, we support prefix KV caching and scored cache entries; that often reduces cost and latency significantly. note: caching interacts with quantization — we ensure the cache key encodes the qprofile variant so we don't serve an INT8 cached token to an FP8 request.
12:00 Ethan: kicking off the sensitivity sweep in the sandbox now — you'll see a progress bar and we'll generate three visualizations: heatmap, latency distribution, and per-prompt delta table.
13:30 Ethan: while that runs, quick deep-dive on qprofiles: qprofile is a bundle with bitwidth, kernel choice, micro-batch size, and KV precision. it's versioned and you can pin per-route and do A/B.
14:20 Sara: do you expose raw kernel metrics? our infra team wants to know GPU utilization, memory footprint, and flop counts ideally.
14:35 Ethan: we expose GPU utilization, memory, and per-call token breakdown in the Console traces. flop counts are provided in the model profile export. if you need deeper telemetry we can add custom tracing via tracing hooks.
15:10 Ethan: sweep is at 40% now. I'm going to show one of the heatmap snapshots. so x axis is p95 latency bins, y axis is drop in intent F1, colors are percent of prompts that land in bucket.
15:44 Ethan: looks like for our triage set, INT8 gives p95 ~150ms and median ~60ms, with about 12% of prompts showing >5% drop in F1. FP8 gives p95 ~210ms but drops only 2% of prompts >5% F1 loss.
16:10 Sara: 12% is high for us. which prompts trigger failure?
16:18 Ethan: mostly those with dense numeric relationships, e.g., "glucose 270" combined with subtle negations. we'll export the example list and annotate.
17:02 Maya: two levers: you can either accept INT8 for triage if you can tolerate a small error band and add a fallback for outliers, or keep FP8 for triage and optimize batching/caching to meet latency.
17:30 Dan: what's the cost delta modeled? we need rough monthly delta for expected 2M tokens / day triage load.
17:45 Maya: rough ballpark: INT8 reduces token compute cost by ~40% — for your volume that's a meaningful savings; we'll provide a detailed cost projection in the follow-up.
18:10 Liam: we're also constrained by PHI. can the sandbox run inside our VPC or do you need data to leave?
18:20 Maya: for the sandbox we usually use anonymized samples, but for a dedicated pilot we can run Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. we'll share our SOC2 + iso docs.
19:05 Sara: also curious about rollouts — if we do a canary, how do we measure quality drift in production?
19:20 Ethan: we support per-route golden prompt sets and live sampling; you can attach eval hooks that compute metrics and fire alerts. we also have regression alerts in Redwood Optimize tied to example sets.
20:00 Ethan: sweep finished — i'll share the CSV and heatmaps now. uploading link: https://redwood.example/sandbox/BC-2026/sweep-0421 (note: link is demo only).
20:18 Ethan: CSV summary: 2k prompts, INT8 median latency 58ms, p95 152ms, 12.3% prompts > 5% F1 drop; FP8 median 95ms, p95 212ms, 2.1% prompts > 5% drop. hybrid with fallback (int8 default, escalate if sim < .82) yields p95 ~160ms with 3.2% incidents.
21:00 Sara: hybrid sounds attractive. that metric threshold — is .82 tunable per prompt class?
21:05 Ethan: yes it's tunable per route and you can set class thresholds. the adaptive policy also includes a cooldown to stop flip-flopping.
22:00 Dan: how deterministic are these runs? if we re-run tomorrow do we expect similar numbers?
22:10 Ethan: mostly yes; we account for sampling variance by running multiple seeds. the qprofile sweep can produce confidence intervals.
23:30 Maya: i want to call out operational considerations: you should pick acceptance thresholds for the triage flow (e.g., <3% F1 drop across critical prompts) and decide on budgeted cost savings. we'll work backwards from that.
24:10 Liam: hypothetically, if we cannot accept any drop for high-risk prompts, can we route those to a high-fidelity check only for flagged categories?
24:20 Ethan: absolutely — tagging is supported and you can do rule-based routing (symptom type, patient age, lab presence).
25:00 Speaker 2 (transcription): "what about the rollback if a release causes regressions?"
25:05 Ethan: Console supports immediate rollback to pinned qprofile version. we also recommend canary + automatic fallback policies while you evaluate.
26:40 Sara: any regulatory paperwork we should be aware of for Private deployment? we need encryption at rest, KMS, audit logs, and a contract for data residency.
26:55 Maya: yes that's our Private playbook; we'll attach the compliance packet and our standard security addendum.
28:00 Ethan: i'm going to demo the routing rule creation — simple UI: create rule, match metadata key "route=triage", assign qprofile "int8-latency-fast", else default to "fp8-fidelity". you can set percent traffic and time window for canary.
29:12 Dan: will the routing rule be honored across Dedicated and Hosted?
29:20 Ethan: yes — the logic is part of the control plane so it behaves the same across Hosted, Dedicated or Private with the same API.
30:00 Ethan: quick note on quant kernels: depending on model architecture we pick different kernels — on some models fp8 kernels are newer and may not be as optimized on older driver stacks; that's why we ran the bench on your target infra profile.
31:10 Sara: what if we want to try int8 but are worried about edge cases? propose a step: 1) run sweep 2) pick threshold and pilot 3) 2-week limited production pilot with golden set monitoring.
31:30 Maya: that's the recommended cadence. we'll supply a qprofile proposal repo and script to ingest your golden set.
32:40 Ethan: showing the per-prompt CSV now, highlighting examples that failed — these will be included in the delivery to help you triage.
33:10 Sara: great. also i want to make sure the fallback doesn't double-bill us — i.e., do we pay for both attempts if fallback happens?
33:28 Maya: you billed token-level compute; in a fallback flow you only pay for the final served tokens. we have policies to avoid duplicate billing for the initial cheap scorer — it's light compute. we'll detail billing in the quote.
34:05 Dan: latency SLO with fallback — worst-case p95 might increase if many fallbacks happen. how do you recommend modelling that?
34:18 Ethan: use the hybrid projection we provided — it shows combined latency distribution. you can also use conservative canary percentages to estimate impact.
35:00 Liam: how long to set up Dedicated pilot?
35:10 Maya: for Dedicated, typically 3-6 weeks including infra provisioning and onboarding. for a Hosted sandbox it's immediate. Private (VPC) is 4-8 weeks depending on networking.
36:05 Ethan: quick demo of rollout UI: you can create canary 5% traffic for 48 hours and set automatic rollback if mean F1 drops > 2%.
37:00 Sara: i like the canary idea. i'm concerned about monitoring overhead for our team. do you provide alert templates?
37:10 Ethan: yes, we have alert templates and pre-built dashboards for triage SLOs. you'll get a starter pack.
38:00 Maya: summarizing options — (A) INT8 default for triage + fallback (lower cost, small error band), (B) FP8 for triage (higher latency/cost, near-zero regression), (C) Hybrid route with rule-based escalation.
38:30 Sara: leaning to hybrid but want to see a 24h bench with our real data first.
38:40 Maya: understood. Ethan, can you run a 24h bench with their data once Sara shares it?
38:48 Ethan: yes i'll queue that — need the dataset and a short acceptance rubric.
39:02 Sara: i'll upload 200 prompts and define thresholds by Friday.
39:10 Ethan: perfect. i'll schedule the run and share results.
39:30 Speaker 3 (transcription): small interruption about a deck share
39:40 Maya: i'll also send the security packet and our pilot pricing estimate.
40:05 Dan: any competitor risk? what do other vendors offer here?
40:12 Ethan: competitors have quant workflows but many don't provide the end-to-end Optimize tooling with routing + KV cache + rollout features baked in. some do offer int8/FP8 comparisons but not the same production controls.
41:00 Sara: timeline — can we do sandbox -> sensitivity sweep -> decision in two weeks?
41:10 Maya: yes that's achievable. plan: D0 sandbox access, D3-7 run bench, D8-10 review, D14 decision.
42:00 Liam: final ask — include a sample compliance addendum and clarifying question on KMS.
42:10 Maya: will do.
43:00 Ethan: last demo note: the Console also shows token-level heatmaps by user route and you can export a QProfile as JSON for auditing.
44:20 Sara: thanks this was helpful.
45:00 Maya: recap of next steps: Maya to share sandbox access, security docs, and pricing; Ethan to run 24h bench when prompts are uploaded; Sara to provide prompt set + thresholds; follow-up in one week to review bench.
45:30 Liam: thanks everyone, we'll be in touch.
45:40 Ethan: thanks all.
---
Post-meeting notes: uploaded sweep artifacts to demo link above; included a short annotated example list for BlueCrest. Some transcription artifacts present (e.g., K V cash -> KV cache, FP8 read as "F P eight" occasionally).
file_notes: Shared artifacts: sandbox heatmap link (demo), security packet to be attached, qprofile export examples. Customer requested 200 triage prompts and acceptance thresholds. Medium transcription quality with occasional speaker labeling issues.
